$comment: Provider config — the single source of truth for the ADR-0009 vendor allowlist: endpoints, model ids, api-key env names, prices per MTok, per-role fallback chains (ADR-0022), and the named role-chain profiles selected by PROVIDER_PROFILE (ADR-0059). The default profile is the base `roles` block and is deliberately NOT declared here: a non-empty `default` entry is a load-time config fault, since the loader returns the base roles before consulting it. Vendor data lives ONLY here (and the model_configs DB mirror); no .ts file in the engine may name a vendor — the boundary gate enforces it by scanning .ts and not .json. Prices are micro-USD per MTok (1 USD = 1e6 micro-USD, so a $0.50/MTok input price is 500000), PR-reviewed like any model decision. Defaults from SPECS.md §3.4 (2026-08).

openrouter.$comment: ADR-0069: OpenAI-compatible aggregator at /v1 — chat completions, embeddings, and (via schema-constrained structured output, the response_format json_schema strict beta) the decision seam of ADR-0042 all ride one key. Paid prepaid-credit terms under the aggregator's published DPA, accepted by the owner 2026-11-14 with zero-retention enabled (dated record: docs/GDPR-ARTICLE-30-RECORD.md §8). Listed prices below are the adopted listings at migration; the aggregator routes per request across upstream endpoints, so some models carry a listing spread — the recorded price names the adopted listing, and an off-listing answer over- or under-records visibly on the trace.

google/gemini-embedding-001.$comment: The SAME Google model id the corpus was embedded with (ADR-0036 gate winner): the embedding space is the model's, so the stored vectors stay valid — no re-embed. The wire sends `dimensions: 1536`; the store rejects any other length loudly (CORPUS_EMBEDDING_DIM), so forwarding must be verified against the corpus before serving.

google/gemini-embedding-2.$comment: Benchmark challenger for the embedder-candidates role — explicitly cross-lingual; embedding-space-incompatible with embedding-001, so adopting it is a clean-slate re-embed, never an upgrade.

google/gemini-3.8-flash.$comment: Mid-tier listing ($0.825 in / $4.125 out per MTok). The cheap-role challenger tail and the provisional `decision` head pending the ADR-0042 bench re-pass — serving flips to the bench's winner by config alone.

deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash.$comment: Decision-bench challenger (ADR-0042): the `decide` capability marks this row a candidate the multilingual gate compares — under the rewritten seam the typing rides schema-constrained chat output, so the capability list — not a vendor protocol — decides what the decider may construct. Not wired to any serving role. Priced at the vendor's published peak rate ($0.30 in / $1.20 out per MTok), the same listing the ollama-cloud row records for this model.

deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash.$comment: Priced at the DeepInfra listing ($0.09 in / $0.18 out per MTok), inside the aggregator's $0.05–$0.21 in / $0.10–$0.56 out endpoint spread; routing is per request unless pinned by a provider preference.

ollama-cloud.$comment: Ollama Cloud Pro on paid terms — OpenAI-compatible at /v1, so the existing chat-completions adapter serves it with no new adapter. Selected ONLY by a profile (see `profiles`); the default chains stay on the aggregator. Terms promise zero data retention, never logged, never trained on; NO signed DPA is on file — the owner accepted that basis for personal data, and the register (docs/GDPR-ARTICLE-30-RECORD.md §8) and ADR-0059 state the absence rather than implying an agreement.

deepseek-v4.1-flash.$comment: Priced at the vendor's published peak rate ($0.30 in / $1.20 out per MTok); off-peak halves. The peak rate is recorded so a cost line must never understate the invoice.

generator.$comment: Cost posture decided 2026-09-12 (ADR-0009): the answer generator runs on the cheap tier — DeepSeek V4-Flash through the aggregator at $0.09/$0.18 per MTok vs Qwen3.7-Max's $2.50/$7.50 — because the trust invariant is carried by the deterministic citation gate and the reviewer gate, not by generator price. The Qwen3.7-Max tail was REMOVED 2026-09-12 (owner decision): DashScope is not provisioned and will not be, and resolveRole silently filters candidates whose apiKeyEnv is unset — so the chain advertised a failover that could never be wired. Single candidate, accepted single point of failure: a generator failure costs one <=$1 smoke re-run, not data. Re-adding a fallback means adding a candidate whose key is actually bound.

reviewer.$comment: Personal-data posture (ADR-0043 decision 3, #181; reviewer re-headed 2026-09-21 per owner): the serving reviewer's prompt embeds the user's question and the drafted answer, so with PromptSpec.personalData required on every serving call only a paid candidate may serve. The designed head was kimi:kimi-k2.6 (cross-vendor, ADR-0009/ADR-0015), but the owner holds no Moonshot key and elected (issue #181 thread) to head the reviewer with the generator model instead. This accepts same-vendor review — the property ADR-0015 named 'anti-self-review' is relaxed for the current key set, recorded as a deliberate trade-off rather than drifted into. Revisit when a second paid vendor key (kimi, qwen) is provisioned.

reviewer-live.$comment: Same head as the reviewer chain.

cheap.$comment: Router stages 1-3, tagging, cleaning. Both candidates ride the aggregator row (ADR-0069): the DeepSeek head answers the personal-data calls, the Gemini Flash tail is the cheap challenger. The retired free-tier tail was the personal-data filter's wired trap case; the filter's correctness is carried by its synthetic unit tests, and no serving chain holds a free-tier candidate anymore (ADR-0009's free-tier policy stays policy, not config).

embedder.$comment: Decided by the #9 embedding benchmark gate (ADR-0036): the chain holds the gate's winner only — never both models, they are embedding-space-incompatible. Served through the aggregator row (ADR-0069) on the SAME model id the corpus was embedded with: the space is the model's, the stored vectors stay valid, no re-embed. The serving retriever embeds the user's sub-queries (personal data): the row is paid and DPA-covered (register rule, ADR-0043). Requires OPENROUTER_API_KEY to be bound, and the dimensions forwarding verified against the corpus before serving.

embedder-candidates.$comment: #9 gate benchmark role: every candidate the benchmark compares, in one chain. Not for serving — the benchmark resolves each candidate directly from this chain (ADR-0022). The benchmark embeds gate-fixture text, never personal data.

decision-candidates.$comment: ADR-0042 decision-bench role (mirrors embedder-candidates): every decision-model candidate the multilingual gate compares — schema-constrained chat candidates through the aggregator's structured output since the ADR-0042 rewrite. Not for serving — the bench resolves each candidate directly. Absent key = the bench reports NOT RUN and exits 0 (CI has no OPENROUTER_API_KEY).

decision.$comment: The decision-model SERVING role (ADR-0042 adoption): the candidate behind the reviewer pre-gate and the retrieval rerank — the model a committed multilingual gate report adopted. Separate from the bench-only `decision-candidates` role so a re-bench can add challengers without changing what serves. The head is PROVISIONAL at the aggregator migration (ADR-0069): the ADR-0042 re-pass bench is the owner's hand-run gate, and its committed report is what flips `benchAdoption` to "committed". Until then the boot posture report names the gate provisional at every boot. Always active wherever OPENROUTER_API_KEY is bound; absent key = neither adoption is wired and the reviewer and retrieval behave as they did before adoption — no enable/disable flag exists. Batched: one call per answer for the pre-gate, one per retrieval whose fused set has two or more candidates for the rerank, input-priced.
